# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊]

I see the bomb. Let me lay out exactly what's printed on it, because I'm the only one who can see any of this.

**Bomb display:** DISPLAY shows `9`. LIGHT is `red`.
**STRIP:** painted `green`, `yellow`, `yellow` (three segments, in that order).
**KEYPAD:** engraved positions `1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8]`, and it reports `[1 digits]` entered, `[entered nothing]`.
**WIRES:** `1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]`.

Now, what did I receive? I hear nothing, so all I got were gestures.

Mute gestured to me twice, identical: `✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌`. That's 6 fists, 4 victory signs, 3 OK signs. Blind gestured a single `✊`.

I need to be careful here. I'm Deaf — I can't hear speech, and I can't touch the bomb. My job is to get what I *see* to the ones who can use it. Blind can touch but can't see; Mute can read the manual but can't speak or touch. So the manual (Mute) plus my eyes must combine, and Blind does the physical work.

The gestures I received are just symbols to me — I don't yet know what they mean. Mute is the one with the manual, so Mute's gesture is probably an encoding of something from the manual. But I can't decode it alone. The key issue: Mute can read the manual but can't speak; I can speak (to Mute and Blind) but can't hear. So Mute can only reach me by gesture, and I can only reach Mute/Blind by speech.

Wait — critically — **Blind cannot see gestures.** So Mute's gestures to me are invisible to Blind, and my speech reaches both Mute and Blind. So I am the bridge: Mute→(gesture)→me→(speech)→Blind.

Let me just describe what I see, plainly, to both Mute and Blind, so the manual-holder can interpret. I'll read out every marking. I'll also relay the gestures I received so that Blind knows Mute sent something (though Blind won't get the symbols), and so Mute knows I got them.

I should describe the bomb fully and ask Mute to tell me what the manual says about these features. I'll send it as speech to both.

Let me also note: the strip has two yellows and a green; wires include yellow, green, red, etc. The keypad has engraved digits 1,5,2,8 at positions 1-4. Display 9, light red.

I'll speak to Mute and Blind describing everything, and gesture to Mute (since Mute can see gestures) to confirm receipt / ask for the manual's mapping. Actually gestures only reach Mute. Let me gesture a simple acknowledgment to Mute and ask via speech.

I'll keep it literal and clear.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. DISPLAY shows 9. LIGHT is red. STRIP painted green yellow yellow in that order. KEYPAD engraved position 1 is 1, position 2 is 5, position 3 is 2, position 4 is 8, and it shows 1 digits entered, entered nothing. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. I received your gestures twice: six fist, four victory, three ok. I do not know what they mean. Tell me what the manual says.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. DISPLAY shows 9. LIGHT is red. STRIP painted green yellow yellow in that order. KEYPAD engraved position 1 is 1, position 2 is 5, position 3 is 2, position 4 is 8, and it shows 1 digits entered, entered nothing. WIRES: 1 yellow, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 green. Mute has sent me gestures I cannot yet decode. Do not touch anything yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [yellow]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👎 🫸]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👎 🫸]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌]

The board changed. Let me note the differences carefully.

**Turn 1:** DISPLAY `9`, LIGHT `red`.
**Turn 2:** DISPLAY `3`, LIGHT `yellow`.

Everything else is identical: STRIP still green/yellow/yellow, KEYPAD same engravings and still `[1 digits] [entered nothing]`, WIRES unchanged.

So the display and light are *live readings* — they change between turns. That's important: the display isn't a fixed marking, it's a state. The light color tracks something too (red→yellow).

New gestures:
- Mute → me (twice, identical): `🫴 👎 🫸` — that's "palm up / thumbs down / rightwards push". Three distinct symbols, repeated, so it's deliberate.
- Blind → me: `✊ ✌` — fist, victory. Two symbols this time (was one fist last turn).

I still can't decode Mute's gestures without the manual's mapping, and I can't hear anything. But I now have a strong clue: Mute repeated the *same* three-symbol gesture twice, and last turn repeated a 13-symbol gesture twice. Repetition suggests Mute is re-sending because I haven't confirmed understanding — or Mute is giving me a key.

Wait. Let me think about the structure. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. Mute's only output to me is gestures. The manual presumably maps bomb features to actions. Mute is trying to tell me something and I keep not decoding it.

Key realization: **Blind gestured `✊ ✌`** — but Blind cannot see gestures, so Blind's gestures are Blind's *own* way of signaling to me... but I'm Deaf, I can see gestures. Actually anyone can gesture; gestures are received by whoever can see. Blind can gesture (hands work) even though Blind can't see. So Blind is using gestures as a channel to me too.

But here's the trap: **I am the only one who both sees gestures AND can speak.** Mute's gestures and Blind's gestures both land on me. My speech lands on Mute and Blind. So I'm the hub.

What do I actually need? I need the manual's rule. Mute has it. Mute is gesturing. I should tell Mute plainly: I don't know the gesture alphabet's meaning — describe the manual's instruction in a way I can relay, or better, since Mute can't speak, Mute must encode via gestures and I must decode. But I have no decoder.

Hmm — maybe the gestures aren't a code I need to crack; maybe they're Mute *spelling* using the gesture alphabet as a symbol set, and the meaning is that Mute is pointing at features. `🫴 👎 🫸` could be "palm-up, thumbs-down, push-right" = a physical manipulation instruction meant for Blind, relayed through me.

Actually the cleanest move: I describe the new live readings (display 3, light yellow) and relay the raw gestures to Blind via speech (Blind can't see gestures but can hear my speech). And I ask Mute to confirm the manual's mapping. I'll also gesture back to Mute to acknowledge and to ask.

Let me speak the full current state and the raw gesture symbols by name, so both Mute and Blind get it. Blind especially needs the readings since Blind can't see them.

I'll gesture to Mute: acknowledge, and ask Mute to repeat the manual rule. But I can't form a question in gestures meaningfully. I'll gesture a simple "received" and rely on speech.

Let me send.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: DISPLAY now shows 3, LIGHT now yellow. Strip, keypad and wires unchanged from before. Your gesture this turn was palm-up, thumbs-down, push-right, sent twice. I still do not know what your gestures mean. I cannot read the manual. Please describe the manual rule in words I can relay, or gesture the mapping slowly. What does the manual say to do?")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: DISPLAY now shows 3, LIGHT now yellow. Strip still green yellow yellow. Keypad engraved 1,5,2,8 with 1 digits entered, entered nothing. Wires 1 yellow 2 white 3 blue 4 red 5 purple 6 green. Mute sent me palm-up, thumbs-down, push-right twice. You sent me fist, victory. Do not touch anything yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [2]
LIGHT [red]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ ✌]

New turn. Let me track the live readings across all three turns:

- **Turn 1:** DISPLAY `9`, LIGHT `red`
- **Turn 2:** DISPLAY `3`, LIGHT `yellow`
- **Turn 3:** DISPLAY `2`, LIGHT `red`

Strip, keypad, wires: unchanged every turn. So the only moving parts are DISPLAY and LIGHT.

Now the gestures. Let me tally Mute's gestures by turn:

- **Turn 1:** `✊×6 ✌×4 👌×3` (13 symbols)
- **Turn 2:** `🫴 👎 🫸` (3 symbols)
- **Turn 3:** `✊×5 ✌×3 👌×4` (12 symbols)

And Blind's:

- **Turn 1:** `✊`
- **Turn 2:** `✊ ✌`
- **Turn 3:** `✊ ✌ ✌`

Interesting. **Blind's gesture count is growing by one each turn: 1, 2, 3 symbols.** That looks like a *counter* — Blind is telling me something is incrementing. Blind can't see, so Blind must be counting something Blind can *feel*. But Blind can't touch yet (nothing entered). Hmm, or Blind is just signaling "turn number."

Now Mute: turns 1 and 3 are pure ✊/✌/👌 counts. Turn 2 was different symbols. Let me look at the counts:

- Turn 1: ✊=6, ✌=4, 👌=3
- Turn 3: ✊=5, ✌=3, 👌=4

Notice: ✊ went 6→5, ✌ went 4→3, 👌 went 3→4. The display went 9→3→2. Hmm.

Actually, wait. Let me reconsider. Maybe Mute's three symbol types encode three *quantities* from the manual, and the counts are the values. In turn 1: 6, 4, 3. Turn 3: 5, 3, 4.

I genuinely cannot decode this without the manual. I've now spent two turns asking Mute to describe the rule and gotten only more gestures. There's a real risk here: **I am the hub, and I may be the bottleneck.** Mute can only output gestures; I can only output speech. Blind can only output gestures and receive speech.

Critical insight I may have been missing: **Mute cannot hear me either? No — Mute can hear.** Mute's "cannot" is speak and touch. Mute CAN hear. So my speech reaches Mute. Good. And Blind can hear my speech. So my speech reaches both.

But Mute's gestures reach only me (Mute→Deaf, and Mute→Blind? No: Blind cannot see, so Mute's gestures do NOT reach Blind). So the manual's content must flow: Mute →(gesture)→ me →(speech)→ Blind.

So Mute is gesturing the manual's instruction to me, expecting me to relay it to Blind as speech. That means **I should relay Mute's gestures verbatim as speech to Blind** — describe each symbol by name — rather than trying to interpret them. Blind can then act on the described manipulation.

That's the key. I've been asking Mute to "explain," but Mute IS explaining — in gestures — and my job is to *transcribe* them into words for Blind. Let me do that now: read out the exact gesture sequence symbol by symbol to Blind.

Mute's turn-3 gesture: `✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌` = "fist fist fist fist fist, victory victory victory, ok ok ok ok."

I'll relay that to Blind as speech, and also relay the current readings. And I'll gesture to Mute to confirm I'm transcribing.

Let me also relay Blind's growing gesture to Mute? Mute can see Blind's gestures? Mute can see — yes, Mute can see gestures. So Mute already sees Blind's gestures. Fine.

Let me send the transcription to Blind.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Relaying Mute's gesture exactly, symbol by symbol: fist, fist, fist, fist, fist, victory, victory, victory, ok, ok, ok, ok. That is five fists, three victories, four oks. Also current readings: DISPLAY shows 2, LIGHT is red. Strip green yellow yellow. Keypad engraved 1,5,2,8, 1 digits entered, entered nothing. Wires 1 yellow 2 white 3 blue 4 red 5 purple 6 green.")
speak(to="mute", text="I am transcribing your gestures to Blind as words. This turn I read: five fists, three victories, four oks. Last turn: palm-up, thumbs-down, push-right. First turn: six fists, four victories, three oks. If these are manual instructions for Blind, keep sending them and I will relay each one. Tell me if I should relay the counts or the symbol names.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [green]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊]

New turn. Live readings:

- **T1:** DISPLAY `9`, LIGHT `red`
- **T2:** DISPLAY `3`, LIGHT `yellow`
- **T3:** DISPLAY `2`, LIGHT `red`
- **T4:** DISPLAY `3`, LIGHT `green`

LIGHT has now shown red, yellow, red, green — all four colors. DISPLAY has shown 9, 3, 2, 3.

Gestures:
- **Mute T4:** `✊×5 ✌×3 👌×4` — *identical to T3.* Same 12-symbol sequence.
- **Blind T4:** `✊` — back to one fist (was 1, 2, 3, now 1 again).

Let me think hard about what's actually going on, because I've been treating my job as transcription, but I should test that.

Blind's gesture count went 1, 2, 3, then back to 1. That's not a monotonic counter — it resets. Combined with the LIGHT cycling red→yellow→red→green and DISPLAY bouncing 9→3→2→3, this smells like a **cycle** or a **state machine**, and Blind's single-fist reset might mark "back to start."

But more importantly: **Mute's T4 gesture is byte-identical to T3.** Mute is not adding new information — Mute is *repeating*. Either Mute is stuck, or Mute is re-sending because I haven't acted on it, or — and this is the crucial possibility — **Mute is repeating because the correct answer is the same, and Mute is waiting for me to relay it to Blind so Blind acts.**

I have not yet caused Blind to do anything. Nothing has been entered (`[entered nothing]`, `[1 digits]` unchanged). The bomb is still armed and untouched. If the intended flow is Mute→me→Blind, then the bottleneck is that **Blind hasn't acted**, and I keep talking instead of delivering an actionable instruction.

But I cannot invent an instruction. I can only relay. And I've relayed the raw symbols. Blind hears "five fists, three victories, four oks" — which is meaningless to Blind too, because Blind doesn't hold the manual either.

So who holds the manual? **Mute.** Mute knows the rule. Mute cannot speak. Mute can gesture to me. I can speak to Blind. The manual's *meaning* has to survive the trip. Raw symbol names don't carry meaning unless Mute and I share a code — and we don't, because I have no manual.

Therefore the only way this works: **the gesture symbols themselves ARE the manual's vocabulary**, and Mute is spelling out a manipulation that Blind can perform by feel. The symbols map to physical actions on the bomb (push, pull, twist, press). Blind can feel the bomb's parts; if I describe "push the thing on the right," Blind can do it.

`🫴 👎 🫸` from T2 fits this beautifully: palm-up (lift/turn up), thumbs-down (press down), push-right (slide right). Those are *physical verbs*. The ✊/✌/👌 counts are less obviously physical, but ✊ (grip), ✌ (two fingers), 👌 (pinch) are also hand actions.

I think I've been overcomplicating. Let me stop trying to decode and instead **give Blind the most actionable relay possible**, and simultaneously **ask Mute for a clearer physical instruction** — and critically, tell Mute that I will relay whatever Mute sends, and that Blind is ready to act but needs a physical instruction, not counts.

Also — I should consider that the gestures might be directed at a *specific part*. The bomb has: strip (3 segments), keypad (4 engraved positions), wires (6). Mute's counts (5/3/4, or 6/4/3) could be **indices**: e.g., "wire 5, wire 3, wire 4" or "position 6, 4, 3." Six wires! T1 had ✊×6 — that's exactly the wire count. Hmm, but T3/T4 have ✊×5.

Let me just lay out the raw data for Blind and ask Mute directly, in speech (Mute hears me), to confirm whether the symbols are indices or actions. I'll keep relaying.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your gesture this turn is identical to last turn: five fists, three victories, four oks. Nothing has been entered on the keypad and nothing has been touched. Blind is ready to act but needs a physical instruction, not a count. Are your symbols indices into the wires, the keypad, or the strip? Or are they physical actions like push, pull, twist, press? Please answer plainly if you can, or send one short gesture sequence that means a single physical action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current readings: DISPLAY shows 3, LIGHT is green. Strip green yellow yellow. Keypad engraved 1,5,2,8, 1 digits entered, entered nothing. Wires 1 yellow 2 white 3 blue 4 red 5 purple 6 green. Mute repeated the same gesture as last turn: five fists, three victories, four oks. I am asking Mute whether these are wire or keypad indices or physical actions. Hold until I relay a clear instruction.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫴", "🫴"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [5]
LIGHT [blue]
STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow]
KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] [1 digits] [entered nothing]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌]

New turn. Live readings:

- **T1:** DISPLAY `9`, LIGHT `red`
- **T2:** DISPLAY `3`, LIGHT `yellow`
- **T3:** DISPLAY `2`, LIGHT `red`
- **T4:** DISPLAY `3`, LIGHT `green`
- **T5:** DISPLAY `5`, LIGHT `blue`

LIGHT has now cycled red, yellow, red, green, blue. DISPLAY: 9, 3, 2, 3, 5.

**Mute's gesture changed this turn.** T3 and T4 were identical (`✊×5 ✌×3 👌×4`). Now T5 is:

`👋 ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✌ 👌 👌 👌 👌`

That's a **new leading symbol: 👋 (waving hand)**, then the same `✊×5 ✌×3 👌×4` tail. So Mute *prepended* a wave to the same sequence.

That's a real signal: Mute is responding to me. I asked "are these indices or actions? send one short gesture." Mute added 👋 at the front. 👋 is a wave — could mean "no," "attention," "hello," or a *waving/moving* action. But the fact that the tail is unchanged suggests 👋 is a **modifier** on the existing sequence, not a replacement.

Blind: `✊ ✌` — two symbols (was 1,2,3,1, now 2). Still cycling.

Let me reconsider the whole picture with fresh eyes, because I think the pattern is now visible.

**The LIGHT cycles through colors, and DISPLAY changes with it.** The strip is painted green/yellow/yellow. The wires are yellow/white/blue/red/purple/green. The light has shown red, yellow, red, green, blue — these are exactly wire colors (red, yellow, green, blue all appear in the wire list!). 

And DISPLAY values: 9, 3, 2, 3, 5. Hmm.

**New idea:** Maybe the LIGHT color *tells us which wire*, and DISPLAY tells us *something about it*. Light red → wire 4 (red). Light yellow → wire 1 (yellow). Light green → wire 6 (green). Light blue → wire 3 (blue). And DISPLAY could be a countdown or a target.

But I can't be sure, and I have no manual. My job remains: get information to the people who can use it.

**The most important thing I notice: Mute is now actively modifying gestures in response to my questions.** Mute added 👋. I should treat Mute's gesture stream as the manual's content and keep relaying it faithfully to Blind, while flagging changes.

But I'm worried I'm still missing the actual mechanism. Let me step back to the *rules of the world*:

- Deaf (me): sees bomb, cannot hear, cannot touch.
- Mute: reads manual, cannot speak, cannot touch.
- Blind: touches bomb, cannot see.

For the bomb to be defused, **Blind must physically act.** Blind can only learn what to do from *my speech* (since Mute can't speak and Blind can't see gestures). So the entire manual must pass Mute→gesture→me→speech→Blind. **I am the sole bridge.** If I relay wrong, everyone dies. If I relay nothing, we never act.

So the correct behavior is: **relay Mute's gestures to Blind as literally and completely as possible, every turn, and let Blind act.** I've been adding my own speculation, which is fine for my thinking, but my *speech to Blind* must be a faithful, unambiguous transcription.

The problem: Blind hears "five fists, three victories, four oks, and a wave." That's still not a physical instruction. Unless... **the gestures ARE the instruction and Blind knows the mapping** — but Blind has no manual, so Blind can't know it either.

Wait — re-read the rules. "A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced." And "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something." **This is the crux.** The gestures are arbitrary until *we agree* on a meaning. Mute and I must *establish a code*. Mute is sending symbols; I must propose an interpretation and confirm it with Mute, then relay the agreed meaning to Blind.

So the productive move is to **propose a concrete mapping and ask Mute to confirm or correct.** I'll propose: the counts correspond to wire numbers / keypad positions, and ask Mute yes/no via gesture.

Actually, simplest and most robust: ask Mute to answer **yes/no** questions with a single gesture (e.g., 👌 = yes, 👎 = no), then I can extract the manual one bit at a time and relay to Blind. That converts Mute's manual into something I can actually transmit.

Let me propose that protocol explicitly, and relay current state to Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New protocol so I can relay your manual to Blind. Answer my questions with one gesture: ok means yes, thumbs-down means no. Question one: does the bomb get defused by cutting exactly one wire? Question two: is the wire to cut the one whose colour matches the LIGHT? This turn LIGHT is blue, so that would be wire 3. Please answer yes or no to each.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current readings: DISPLAY shows 5, LIGHT is blue. Strip green yellow yellow. Keypad engraved 1,5,2,8, 1 digits entered, entered nothing. Wires 1 yellow 2 white 3 blue 4 red 5 purple 6 green. Mute added a wave symbol before the same sequence: wave, five fists, three victories, four oks. I am setting up a yes/no protocol with Mute so I can relay the manual to you clearly. Hold.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
